title: Rotate Array
description:
Rotate an array to the right by k positions: every element moves k places to the right and the elements that fall off the end wrap around to the front.

Input format
Line 1: n and k separated by a space.
Line 2: n integers.

Output format
The rotated array on one line, values separated by single spaces.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000. 0 <= k <= 1000000000 (k can be larger than n). Values fit in a 32-bit signed integer.
hints: What happens to the array if you rotate it by exactly n positions? Use that to shrink k.
After replacing k with k mod n, the last k elements move to the front and the rest follow them.
Result = a[n-k:] + a[:n-k] after k = k % n. Be careful when k % n is 0: a[-0:] is the whole array in Python.

examples.explanation: Rotating right by 2 moves the last two values, 4 and 5, to the front.
Rotating by 4 is the same as rotating by 4 mod 3 = 1.
